hook.text: Every known culture forbids some form of incest. It's the most universal of all human taboos. But why?

buildup.text: The incest taboo forbids sexual relations and marriage between certain close relatives, but the exact rules vary.

discovery.text: Theories include avoiding inbreeding, maintaining family roles, and forcing people to marry out and build alliances.

twist.text: Egyptian pharaohs and Hawaiian royals practiced sibling marriage. Elite incest was used to concentrate sacred power.

climax.text: The incest taboo is universal in existence but variable in scope. It forces outward connections that build society.

punchline.text: The taboo exists everywhere but means different things.

quiz.question: Why is the incest taboo considered significant?
options: It only exists in Western cultures
It's universal and forces outward connections that build society

details.summary: The incest taboo prohibiting sexual relations between close relatives is found in virtually every known society, though cultures define prohibited relationships differently. It is one of the few near-universal cultural rules identified by anthropologists.
details.whyItMatters: The incest taboo sits at the intersection of biology and culture. Its near-universality raises fundamental questions about whether some cultural rules have biological roots and why human societies regulate sexuality.
takeaways: The incest taboo is found in virtually all known human societies
Different cultures define prohibited relationships differently
It is one of the few near-universal cultural rules

faq.question: Why is the incest taboo considered nearly universal?
faq.answer: Every documented society prohibits sexual relations between some category of close relatives, though which relatives are included varies. Biological explanations cite inbreeding depression. Social explanations, following Lévi-Strauss, argue it forces outmarriage and creates alliances.

faq.question: Do all cultures define incest the same way?
faq.answer: No. Some societies prohibit marriage between parallel cousins but encourage cross-cousin marriage. Others extend the taboo to clan members who may not be biologically related. The biological core is consistent, but the cultural boundaries vary significantly.
